method: Evidence pack from the release file; one Sonnet 5.5 agent established the facts with exact quotes; every quote checked against the release files and README by script; the facts that set the level checked again by hand; level from the fixed rule; label and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
label: Downloads and runs Python with an alignment model (194 MB) when you press install, on Windows
summary: On Windows (x64), when you press the one-click button to install the local alignment model, it downloads about 194 MB, as its README says: Python from python.org, three Python packages from PyPI, and a word-alignment model, a data file, from the Hugging Face account cstr. It then runs that Python on the plugin's own script.

facts.what: On Windows x64 only, downloads seven files totalling 194,108,801 bytes: the embeddable Python 3.12.10 zip (11.1 MB) from python.org, wheels for numpy, onnxruntime and tokenizers from files.pythonhosted.org (30.3 MB), and an int8 ONNX word-alignment model (149.7 MB), tokenizer.json and README from the Hugging Face repo cstr/awesome-align-onnx-int8. It unpacks them into the Zotero cache and then runs the downloaded python.exe (isolated mode, -I) on the plugin's own alignment-worker.py to test and later use the model.
facts.publisher: python.org and PyPI, where Python and those packages are published
facts.readmeQuote: Optional offline ONNX alignment can be installed with the one-click installer on Windows x64 (about 194 MB from Python.org, PyPI and Hugging Face).

facts.notes: The scanner's 'checksum from the same source' is wrong here: the addresses and the expected SHA-256 and byte size of every file are written in the plugin's own code (installAssets array, biread.js ~20067-20125), not fetched from the server. install() (20189) downloads each file to a .part file via Downloads.createDownload({source: asset.url}) (20231), compares size and sha256(part) to asset.sha256 and throws '校验失败' (verification failed) on mismatch (20244-20245), and only then moves/unpacks it. Addresses are fixed constants: none comes from a setting, manifest or server reply. Hugging Face URLs are pinned to commit e803a2f5... ; the PyPI URLs are exact file paths. Trigger: the 'AnnotationControls' constructor adds a settings button labelled \u4E00\u952E\u5B89\u88C5\u672C\u5730\u6A21\u578B ('one-click install local model') whose handler calls installLocalModel(); its tooltip says 'Windows x64: first download about 194 MB, auto-configured and verified'. Nothing calls installLocalModel automatically (only caller is that click handler, line ~20310). On non-Windows or non-x64 install() throws before any download. Run step: runLocalModel (19523) does Subprocess.call({command: configuration.python, arguments: ["-I", worker, configPath]}) where configuration.python is the downloaded python.exe, and install() itself calls verify() -> runLocalModel right after downloading. So the downloaded Python is executed. The downloaded model file is loaded by onnxruntime inside that Python. 'source' is third-party because the model files come from an unrelated Hugging Face account (cstr), the most concerning of the sources; Python itself (python.org, PyPI wheels from files.pythonhosted.org) is the official source of those projects. Python.org zip is the official Python embeddable build. Note the plugin also has a manual-config button that lets the user pick their own local-model.json (python/model/deps absolute paths) but that downloads nothing. README says about 194 MB from Python.org, PyPI and Hugging Face, and that downloads are checksum-verified; size sum of the installAssets bytes = 194,108,801 matches. Not a fork recorded in pack; code is a fork of zotero-pdf-translate but the installer is BiRead's own.
facts.reviewerNote: Source recorded as official for the programs that run (python.org, PyPI); the model files come from the Hugging Face account cstr, pinned to a commit and by SHA-256, and are data loaded by onnxruntime. Checked by hand: every address, size and SHA-256 is in installAssets (biread.js ~20067-20125) and install() refuses a mismatch (line 20244); the numpy, onnxruntime and tokenizers hashes equal PyPI's published digests (checked 2026-10-16).
